climate.overview_html: The defining new climate signal on September 2 is the ENSO picture: NOAA CPC’s August ENSO diagnostic confirms the Niño 3.4 index reached +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — with 15 coupled-model ensemble members projecting the index to exceed +3.0°C at the September–November peak, a threshold that would formally classify this as a “Super El Niño” rivaling the 2015–16 event; NOAA assigns >90% probability to a “very strong” event this autumn and sees no transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. This intensification directly underlies the hyperactive Eastern/Central Pacific season (three simultaneous named storms), WWA’s attribution finding that the European 2026 heat and drought was “virtually impossible” without climate change (2.5°C anthropogenic amplification), and JRC EFFIS’s EU wildfire burnt area of 634,473 ha — 33% above the same date in the record 2025 season. The cascade of 2026 summer extremes prompted Chatham House to designate climate change as Europe’s primary systemic security threat, backed by 10,000 excess deaths from the June heatwave, 9 M tonnes of crop losses, and military assets diverted from conventional security to fire suppression and flood defense.

items.headline: NOAA August ENSO Diagnostic: Niño 3.4 Reaches +2.7°C Week of August 12; 15 Ensemble Members Forecast Peak >+3.0°C (“Super El Niño” Threshold); >90% Probability “Very Strong” Event Sept–Nov 2026; No La Niña Transition Before Spring 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the ongoing El Niño is now tracking toward historically extreme territory. The Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomaly index reached +2.03°C in July 2026 and +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — already exceeding the +2.5°C threshold for a "very strong" event under NOAA's classification system. All 15 coupled model ensemble members in the multi-model objective ENSO outlook forecast Niño 3.4 exceeding +2.5°C at the September–November peak window; a majority project exceedance of +3.0°C, which would formally qualify this as a "Super El Niño" comparable to the 2015–16 event (+2.6°C peak) and approaching the record 1997–98 event (+3.3°C peak). NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event during September–November 2026 with little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. This ENSO context explains the record global SST of 21.1°C recorded August 22, the hyperactive Pacific season (Karina, Lowell, Marie), and the elevated baseline for Northern Hemisphere extreme heat.

items.headline: WWA Attribution: European 2026 Summer Heat and Drought Would Have Been Virtually Impossible Without Climate Change — 2.5°C Anthropogenic Amplification; Droughts Now More Severe and More Frequent
items.summary: World Weather Attribution's rapid attribution analysis of the summer 2026 European heat and drought concludes that the observed temperature anomalies and rainfall deficits would have been virtually impossible in a pre-industrial climate. Anthropogenic climate change increased temperatures across the affected region by approximately 2.5°C above a pre-industrial summer baseline. The study finds European droughts are becoming both more severe and more frequent, with soil moisture deficits in 2026 reaching levels not previously observed in the instrumental record across parts of central and southern Europe. The findings directly underpin the Chatham House security assessment and support JRC EFFIS data showing European wildfires in 2026 tracking 33% ahead of the previous record year.

items.headline: Climate Change Is Now Europe’s Biggest Systemic Security Threat — 10,000 Excess Deaths From June Heatwave; 9M Tonnes Crop Loss; Military Assets Diverted to Fire Suppression and Flood Defense
items.summary: Chatham House published a policy analysis concluding that climate change is now Europe's biggest systemic security risk. The summer of 2026 provides the evidence base: extreme heat contributed to an estimated 10,000 excess deaths during the June heatwave alone and destroyed approximately 9 million tonnes of crops from the European harvest. The security dimension is direct: prolonged drought contributed to wildfires igniting at Dutch military training grounds; Europe's armed forces are increasingly deployed to fight fires, reinforce flood defenses, evacuate populations, and restore critical infrastructure — diverting personnel and logistics capacity from conventional security operations. Rhine water levels fell to their lowest since 1880. Chatham House argues that climate adaptation investment has structurally lagged behind mitigation spending and that European security planning must treat climate hazard as a primary threat category alongside geopolitical risks.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 634,473 Hectares Burned — 33% Above Same Date in Record 2025 Season; Very-Extreme Fire Danger Through September 2; Rhine at Lowest Since 1880; Danube at Record Low; Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area reached 634,473 hectares as of August 30 — tracking 33% ahead of the same date in the record 2025 season. Very-extreme fire danger indices persist across a broad band running through Romania and Hungary; extreme danger extends to southern Ireland and central-southern Italy through September 2. The Rhine has fallen to its lowest level since 1880, forcing cargo vessels to carry fractional loads and triggering surcharges rippling through German industrial supply chains. The Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. The atmospheric blocking pattern sustaining the Eastern European heat anomaly shows no credible breakdown signal through September 5.

items.headline: US Labor Day Heat Dome: 80M+ Under Extreme/Major Heat Threat Through Early September; Mississippi Valley, Southeast, Mid-Atlantic Focus; 10–15°F Above Normal; Severe Storms Along Ridge Periphery
items.summary: The US heat dome that spent August baking the Desert Southwest and Southern Plains shifted its axis eastward, threatening the Mississippi Valley and mid-Atlantic/Southeast corridor through the first several days of September. Over 30 million people face "extreme" heat conditions; another 50 million are under "major" heat threat. Forecast daytime highs include near-100°F in Raleigh and St. Louis; 90s-plus in Cincinnati, Philadelphia, Atlanta, and Washington D.C., all running 10–15°F above historical averages. The blocking ridge is simultaneously deflecting severe storm systems into the Northeast and Great Lakes. Dallas recorded 27 days at or above 100°F in August 2026, and the Climate Prediction Center flags a slight risk of hazardous heat returning to the Southern US September 7–10.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Explosive Rapid Intensification to Category 4 (130 mph); Forecast ~300 Miles South of Hawaii Late Wednesday–Friday; Dangerous Surf Midweek; Karina Also Entering Central Pacific Thursday — Dual Major Hurricane Hawaii Threat
major_events.status: CATEGORY 4 · 130 MPH · RAPID INTENSIFICATION · HAWAII SOUTH-PASS LATE WED–FRI · DANGEROUS SURF
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell underwent one of the most dramatic rapid intensification sequences ever recorded in the Central Pacific basin, surging from Tropical Storm to Category 4 with maximum sustained winds near 130 mph. The official CPHC/NHC forecast track brings Lowell's center to a closest approach of approximately 300 miles south of Hawaii's Big Island late Wednesday night through Friday. Life-threatening ocean swells will reach east- and southeast-facing Hawaii shores by midweek, and a Lowell-driven pressure gradient may produce trade-wind gusts exceeding 50 mph across some locations. The situation is made historically unusual by the simultaneous approach of Hurricane Karina: Category 4, forecast to enter the Central Pacific late Thursday into Friday. Both major hurricanes approaching Hawaii's latitude simultaneously under Super El Niño sea surface temperatures is an extremely rare dual-storm configuration. Hawaii civil defense authorities are monitoring both systems.

major_events.name: Hurricane Karina (Eastern Pacific / Entering Central Pacific) — Cat 4 (130 mph, Down from 145 mph Peak); Forecast to Enter Central Pacific Late Thursday; No Landfall; Combined Hawaii Dual-Storm Threat With Lowell
major_events.status: CATEGORY 4 · 130 MPH · SLIGHT WEAKENING · ENTERING CENTRAL PACIFIC LATE THURSDAY · DUAL THREAT WITH LOWELL
major_events.impact: Hurricane Karina remains a Category 4 major hurricane with maximum sustained winds near 130 mph as of September 2 advisories — a slight decrease from the 145 mph peak on September 1. Moving west-northwest, Karina is forecast to enter the Central Pacific basin late Thursday night into Friday on a trajectory converging with Lowell's wake in the vicinity of the Hawaiian Islands. NHC forecasts continued gradual weakening over cooler waters, but Karina is expected to remain a significant hurricane through the Hawaii-region passage window. Life-threatening surf and rip-current warnings remain active for southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula. No landfall is forecast.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Marie (Eastern Pacific) — NEW: 13th Named EP Storm of 2026; Formed September 1; Large 160-NM Wind Field; Forecast Hurricane by Wednesday; Three Simultaneous Pacific Systems Under Super El Niño
major_events.status: TROPICAL STORM · INTENSIFYING · FORECAST HURRICANE WED · LARGE WIND FIELD 160 NM RADIUS
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Marie, the 13th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season, formed during the early morning hours of September 1. As of the first advisories, the center was near 15.0°N, 108.7°W, moving northwest at 9 mph. Deep convection with cloud top temperatures of -81°C is developing over the circulation center. Marie has an unusually large wind field: tropical storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 nautical miles over the eastern semicircle. NHC projects intensification to hurricane status by Wednesday night before Marie encounters drier air and cooler waters. With Marie's formation, the 2026 season now carries three active Pacific systems simultaneously — Karina (Cat 4), Lowell (Cat 4), and Marie (Tropical Storm) — an extraordinary situation driven by Super El Niño sea surface temperature anomalies across the Eastern and Central Pacific.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Edouard (Atlantic) — MADE LANDFALL September 1: Johnson Bayou, Louisiana; 60 mph Winds; 5th Named Atlantic Storm of 2026; Flash Flooding Southeast Texas; Now Dissipating
major_events.status: MADE LANDFALL · SEPTEMBER 1 · 60 MPH · JOHNSON BAYOU LA · DISSIPATING
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Edouard, the fifth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, made landfall near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana, at approximately 2:20 p.m. CDT September 1, with maximum sustained winds of 60 mph. The storm formed rapidly — strengthening from a Potential Tropical Cyclone to tropical storm status within 9 hours. Wind gusts reached 71 mph near the Texas-Louisiana border. Despite a compact wind field (tropical storm force extending only 25 miles from center), Edouard's inner core produced rainfall of 2–5 inches per hour, triggering flash flooding across parts of southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana. Edouard is forecast to dissipate by Wednesday night. No casualties have been confirmed.

major_events.name: US Labor Day Heat Dome — Axis on Mississippi Valley, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast Through September 4; 80M+ at Extreme/Major Risk; Raleigh Heat Wave Through Sept 4; Philadelphia Through Sept 3; Severe Storms Along Northeast Periphery
major_events.status: ONGOING · 80M+ AT RISK · SE/MID-ATLANTIC/MIDWEST FOCUS · RALEIGH HEAT WAVE THROUGH SEPT 4
major_events.impact: The US heat dome remains focused on the Mississippi Valley, Southeast, and mid-Atlantic corridor through early September. Daytime highs are running 10–15°F above historical averages. Raleigh faces the event's longest city-level heat wave, spanning September 1–4; Philadelphia's runs September 1–3. Near-100°F highs are forecast in Raleigh and St. Louis; 90s-plus in Cincinnati, Philadelphia, Atlanta, and Washington D.C. The Climate Prediction Center signals a slight risk of hazardous heat returning to the Southern US September 7–10. The blocking ridge continues deflecting severe convective systems into the Northeast and Great Lakes, with multiple rounds of flooding-capable storms expected.

major_events.name: Indonesia / SE Asia / Philippines Wildfire Haze — UPDATE: Haze Affecting Broader Philippines Through September 3; Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa Now Impacted; ASEAN Level 3 Alert; 600+ Malaysian Schools Closed
major_events.status: ASEAN LEVEL 3 · PHILIPPINES THROUGH SEPT 3 · BROADER LUZON IMPACTED · 600+ MALAYSIAN SCHOOLS CLOSED
major_events.impact: The Philippine DENR-EMB confirmed September 1–2 that smoke from Kalimantan fires transported by the southwest monsoon (Habagat) will continue affecting the Philippines through September 3. The impacted geographic footprint has expanded beyond Metro Manila to include Central Luzon, Calabarzon, and Mimaropa. Metro Manila PM2.5 readings remain at "acutely unhealthy" levels: Parañaque (296 AQI), Quezon City (241), Las Piñas (237), Manila (231), and Malabon (229) among the worst. Air quality may improve September 4–6 contingent on wind-pattern shifts or rainfall. The ASEAN Specialized Meteorological Centre's Level 3 alert remains active; over 600 schools in Malaysia's Sarawak remain closed. Drier and warmer than normal conditions are forecast through mid-September.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — 299 Dead Including 140 Children; 715 Injured; NDMA: 2–3 More Monsoon Spells in September; Flash Flood Risk Across All Provinces
major_events.status: ONGOING · 299 DEAD · 140 CHILDREN · PEAK MONSOON SEASON · 2–3 MORE SPELLS FORECAST
major_events.impact: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299, including 140 children, 102 men, and 57 women, per NDMA reporting. An additional 715 people have been injured (239 children). Property damage has affected 1,676 homes, with 562 completely destroyed. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa leads in provincial fatalities, followed by Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, AJK, and Gilgit-Baltistan. NDMA forecasts 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the climatological peak. Flash-flood and heavy-rain advisories continue across all affected provinces.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire and Drought Emergency — 634,473 ha Burned; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed; No Pattern Break Through September 5
major_events.status: ONGOING · 634,473 HA · RHINE LOWEST SINCE 1880 · PAKS OUTPUT CURTAILED · NO BREAK THROUGH SEPT 5
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 634,473 hectares as of August 30, tracking 33% ahead of the same date in the 2025 record season. Very-extreme fire danger persists across the Romania–Hungary corridor; extreme danger extends to southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. Rhine water levels are at their lowest since 1880, spiking inland cargo costs and reducing vessel load capacity. The Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. The blocking pattern shows no credible breakdown signal through September 5.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — HELD Status Maintained; 25,230 Hectares; Phased Re-Entry Ongoing; 150 Structures Damaged; One Fatality; 379 Firefighters Active
major_events.status: HELD · 25,230 HA · PHASED RE-ENTRY ASSESSMENT · 379 FIREFIGHTERS ACTIVE
major_events.impact: BC Wildfire Service's HELD classification for the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland is maintained as of September 2. The fire has burned 25,230 hectares after approximately 26 days of burning. 379 wildland firefighters, 7 helicopters, and 43 pieces of heavy equipment remain assigned. Evacuation orders and alerts remain active for portions of Summerland and Peachland. A phased re-entry assessment is underway for lower-risk zones. The fire has damaged or destroyed approximately 150 structures and claimed one life. Cooler weather and rainfall since August 28 have aided suppression.

weather.overview_html: The headline meteorological development September 2 is Hurricane Lowell’s explosive rapid intensification from Tropical Storm directly to Category 4 (130 mph) — one of the most dramatic intensification sequences recorded in the Central Pacific basin — with a forecast track passing approximately 300 miles south of Hawaii late Wednesday through Friday and dangerous surf reaching east-facing shores by midweek. The Hawaii threat environment is now doubly complex: Category 4 Hurricane Karina, which peaked at 145 mph on September 1, is forecast to enter the Central Pacific late Thursday — both major hurricanes approaching Hawaii’s latitude near-simultaneously under Super El Niño sea surface temperatures, an extremely rare dual-storm scenario. A third Eastern Pacific system, Tropical Storm Marie, formed September 1 as the 13th named EP storm of 2026 with an unusually large 160-NM wind field and a forecast to reach hurricane strength by Wednesday. In the Atlantic, Tropical Storm Edouard made landfall near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana, at 2:20 p.m. CDT September 1 with 60 mph winds and produced flash flooding in southeast Texas before weakening toward dissipation.

items.source: KHON2 / Hawaii News Now / CPHC / NHC

The official CPHC/NHC forecast track brings Lowell's center to a closest approach of approximately 300 miles south of Hawaii's Big Island late Wednesday night through Friday, September 4–5. Life-threatening ocean swells will reach east- and southeast-facing Hawaii shores by midweek, with life-threatening rip currents. A Lowell-generated pressure gradient may also produce trade-wind gusts exceeding 50 mph across some Hawaii locations Wednesday through Friday. The situation is complicated by Hurricane Karina's forecast entry into the Central Pacific late Thursday into Friday — both Category 4 systems approaching Hawaii's latitude near-simultaneously. This dual major hurricane configuration in the Central Pacific, driven by Super El Niño sea surface temperatures, is extremely unusual. Hawaii civil defense is actively tracking both storms and has issued preparatory advisories.

items.source: Fox Weather / CNN / CBS News / KBTX
items.headline: Tropical Storm Edouard Makes Landfall Near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana; 60 mph Winds; 5th Atlantic Storm of 2026; Flash Flooding Southeast Texas; Now Dissipating by Wednesday

Edouard formed rapidly — strengthening from a Potential Tropical Cyclone to tropical storm status within 9 hours. Maximum wind gusts reached 71 mph near the Texas-Louisiana border. The storm's compact size (tropical storm-force winds extending only 25 miles from center) limited the overall footprint, but the inner core delivered rainfall of 2–5 inches per hour across parts of southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana, triggering flash flooding. A tropical storm warning had been in effect from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion-Iberia Parish line. Edouard is forecast to weaken to a tropical depression and fully dissipate by Wednesday night. The landfall occurred during the Labor Day weekend, compounding heat-dome impacts on the Gulf Coast region.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Marie Joins Eastern Pacific as 13th Named Storm of 2026; Super El Niño Sustains Three Simultaneous Pacific Systems; Large 160-NM Wind Field; Forecast Hurricane by Wednesday
items.summary: Tropical Storm Marie formed during the early morning hours of September 1, becoming the 13th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season. The center was near 15.0°N, 108.7°W at formation, moving northwest at 9 mph. Deep convection with cloud top temperatures of -81°C is developing over the circulation center, and a spiral band is wrapping around from the southwest. Marie has an unusually large wind field: tropical storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 nautical miles over the eastern semicircle. NHC projects Marie to intensify to hurricane status by Wednesday night before encountering drier air and cooler waters. With Marie's formation alongside Category 4 Karina and now Category 4 Lowell, the 2026 season runs three simultaneous active Pacific systems — an extraordinary situation driven by Super El Niño sea surface temperature anomalies. The season's hyperactivity also connects to Atlantic Tropical Storm Edouard's simultaneous landfall in Louisiana.

items.headline: Philippines EMB: Kalimantan Haze to Affect Philippines Through September 3; Broader Luzon Regions Now Impacted — Metro Manila, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa; PM2.5 Readings Up to AQI 296

PM2.5 AQI readings reached "acutely unhealthy" levels across multiple Metro Manila cities on September 1: Parañaque (296), Quezon City (241), Las Piñas (237), Manila (231), and Malabon (229). Quezon City suspended in-person classes for all public schools September 1, a measure affecting Child Development Centers through Grade 12. The ASEAN Specialized Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert remains active; over 600 schools in Malaysia's Sarawak remain closed.

renewables.overview_html: Australia entered the offshore wind era on August 25–26 as Victoria launched the country’s first offshore wind auction — tendering 2 GW across two Bass Strait and Southern Ocean zones, with contracts expected in 2028 and a pathway to 9 GW by 2040. In the US, the structural story remains the same: EIA data show solar, wind, and storage added 44,889 MW in the year to June 2026 versus only 7,530 MW for natural gas, with combined renewable installed capacity on pace to surpass the entire gas fleet within ≈12 months; California’s lawsuit over the $120M buyout of the 2 GW Golden State Wind lease illustrates the federal–state collision, while wind and solar have already hit a record 22.3% share of US electrical production in H1 2026 with solar leading monthly generation for the first time in June. In the UK, plug-in residential solar panels became legal under SI 2026/848 from August 27, available at 800+ Argos stores.

items.headline: Victoria Launches Australia’s First Offshore Wind Auction: 2 GW Tendered Across Bass Strait and Southern Ocean Zones; 12-Month RFP Phase; Contracts Expected 2028; Pathway to 9 GW by 2040
items.summary: Victoria launched Australia's first offshore wind auction on August 25–26, opening a 12-month Request for Proposal (RFP) phase for projects to deliver 2 GW of offshore wind generation. The auction covers two declared offshore wind zones in the Bass Strait off Gippsland and the Southern Ocean off western Victoria. Contracts for the first 2 GW are expected to be awarded in 2028 following an evaluation period. The 2 GW round is the first step toward Victoria's 4 GW by 2035 and 9 GW by 2040 targets. Successful projects would generate enough electricity to power approximately 1.5 million homes. The auction launch confirms Australia is now operationalizing offshore wind policy after years of legislative development, positioning Victoria as the lead Australian jurisdiction for commercial offshore wind deployment.

items.headline: California Sues Trump Administration Over $120 Million Deal to Cancel 2 GW Golden State Wind Offshore Lease; Alleges Violations of Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act; $100M in Port/Transmission Prep Already Spent
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission filed suit August 28 against the Trump administration and Golden State Wind, challenging the Interior Department's April 2026 agreement to pay Golden State Wind $120 million to abandon its 2 GW offshore wind lease and invest instead in fossil fuel projects. The complaint alleges violations of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Judgment Fund Act, and other federal statutes, asking the court to void the agreement. The 2 GW project would have supplied clean electricity to more than 1 million California homes. The state notes it has already spent more than $100 million on port upgrades, transmission system improvements, and other infrastructure in preparation for the project.

items.headline: EIA Data: US Renewables Installed Capacity to Surpass Natural Gas Within 12 Months — Solar+Wind Added 44,889 MW vs. Gas’s 7,530 MW in Year to June 2026; Battery Storage Up 17,859 MW
items.summary: New EIA capacity data analyzed by Electrek show US renewable energy installed capacity is on pace to surpass natural gas within approximately 12 months — most likely by summer 2027. In the year through June 30, 2026: utility-scale solar added 28,077 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind added 10,553 MW; combined renewable additions totaled 44,889 MW. Natural gas capacity grew by only 7,530 MW in the same period. Utility-scale battery storage added 17,859 MW. When combined renewables capacity eventually exceeds natural gas's installed base, it will mark a structural inflection in the US power system, though natural gas will continue to provide dispatchability that capacity figures alone do not capture.

items.headline: CleanTechnica Analysis: Renewable Energy Keeps Winning Despite Federal Headwinds — Solar Leads US Monthly Generation for First Time in June 2026; 22.3% of H1 US Production
items.summary: CleanTechnica's analysis of EIA data concludes that neither Trump administration policy, tariff uncertainty, nor offshore wind cancellations have materially slowed the US solar-wind-storage deployment trajectory. Between July 2025 and June 2026: utility-scale solar grew 28,076.7 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind grew 10,552.9 MW. Combined solar and wind provided 22.3% of domestic electrical production in H1 2026. In June 2026, solar-generated electricity exceeded both wind and hydropower output for the month — the first time solar ranked as the leading renewable source for any single calendar month in the US. The analysis frames federal headwinds as causing friction at the margins rather than reversing structural momentum.

items.headline: UK Plug-In Solar Panels Legal Across Great Britain From August 27 — SI 2026/848 Enables 800 W Residential Systems Via Standard Sockets; Available at 800+ Argos Stores; Saves Up to £110/Year
items.summary: Plug-in solar panels became legal for residential use across England, Wales, and Scotland from August 27, 2026, under Plug-In Solar Amendment SI 2026/848. The regulation allows compliant systems with a maximum rated AC output of 800 W (micro-inverter limited) and combined panel rating up to 2,000 W DC to connect to a home's electricity supply via an approved standard plug and socket, without requiring planning permission or a certified electrician. The change creates a legal pathway that has existed in Germany, France, and the Netherlands for several years but was previously unavailable in the UK. The government estimates systems can save households up to £110 per year; systems are immediately available at over 800 Argos stores across Great Britain.

science.overview_html: The freshest arXiv result in the rolling window is arXiv 2608.30795 (August 31), which renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end forecasting system probabilistic by attaching learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder (capturing aleatoric uncertainty from the observing system) and Monte Carlo dropout in the processor (capturing epistemic uncertainty in learned dynamics); the key payoff is that probabilistic fine-tuning also improves the mean forecast by 4.2% across variables and lead times — uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill turn out to be mutually reinforcing. Three papers from the mid-window remain active reference: the “Missing the Butterfly” analysis tracing AIWP’s absent butterfly effect to training-data coarse-graining, with direct implications for how benchmark accuracy claims should be read; NOAA’s Nested-EAGLE, which outperforms both GFS and HRRR for near-surface fields over CONUS in a unified short-and-medium-range architecture; and ECMWF’s AIFL LSTM streamflow model, deployed operationally in Copernicus EMS with the ability to detect a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance — directly relevant as Pakistan and Southeast Asia face ongoing monsoon and wildfire-haze emergencies.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric (Observing System) and Epistemic (Model) Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%; Law-of-Total-Variance Attribution
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper addresses a critical gap in end-to-end AI weather prediction: Aardvark Weather produces skillful global gridded and station forecasts directly from raw Earth observations, replacing the NWP pipeline including data assimilation, but the system is deterministic — issuing no uncertainty estimates. The authors render it probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder, capturing aleatoric uncertainty inherited from the observing system (instrument noise, sparse sampling, temporal gaps); and (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor, capturing epistemic uncertainty in the learned atmospheric dynamics. The resulting nested ensemble attributes forecast spread to the two sources through a law-of-total-variance decomposition, cross-checked by withholding specific observation streams. The key empirical result: probabilistic fine-tuning significantly improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — suggesting that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension. The paper frames the decomposition as essential infrastructure for operational AI weather prediction, where decision-making requires calibrated confidence bounds, not just point forecasts.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.25835: AI Weather Models “Missing the Butterfly” and Skillful Backcasting Traced to Training-Data Coarse-Graining — Physics-Like Properties Recoverable by Reducing Coarse-Graining; Implication for Benchmark Accuracy Claims
items.summary: A paper from the LMU Munich/ECMWF group identifies a unified root cause for two puzzling behaviors of AI weather prediction models: their failure to simulate the butterfly effect (sensitivity to initial-condition perturbations — a fundamental property of atmospheric chaos) and their surprising ability to skillfully backcast (predict the past). The explanation: training data coarse-graining removes fast, small-scale modes, creating a temporally smoothed training distribution in which the model learns to interpolate rather than model true atmospheric dynamics. When coarse-graining is progressively reduced, the arrow of time and butterfly-effect sensitivity re-emerge. The finding has direct consequence for how AIWP benchmark accuracy should be interpreted: some of the accuracy advantage attributed to neural weather models may reflect temporal smoothing rather than genuine dynamical skill.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.26822 (Nested-EAGLE): Single ML System Bridges 0.25° Global and 6-km Regional Forecasting Over CONUS; Lower MSE Than Both GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Fields; Unified Short- and Medium-Range Architecture
items.summary: A NOAA team introduces Nested-EAGLE, an ML weather prediction system that unifies short-range and medium-range forecasting in a single architecture. Nested-EAGLE combines a 0.25° global forecast model with a 6 km refinement over CONUS, incorporating high-resolution regional analysis data into training through the nesting process. Key result: Nested-EAGLE achieves significantly lower mean-squared error in near-surface and low-level quantities over CONUS compared to both GFS and HRRR, while remaining competitive globally. The authors argue that unifying short- and medium-range prediction into a single coherent system would provide the public with an improved distillation of global weather and local impacts, replacing NOAA's current multi-system approach.

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF announced the operational deployment of AIFL (AI for Floods) on August 27, 2026 within the Copernicus Emergency Management Service global flood forecasting component. AIFL is a deterministic LSTM trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset using a two-stage approach: pre-training on 40 years of ERA5-Land reanalysis, then fine-tuned on IFS control forecasts. Independent test performance (2021–2024): median modified KGE′ of 0.66 and median NSE of 0.53 globally. Most operationally significant: AIFL detected a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance during the January 2024 Storm Henk floods in Belgium. The deployment is directly relevant to ongoing flood emergencies in Pakistan and the Philippines.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion in Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%) of Global AAL; 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from its prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss (AAL) figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%. The benchmark rose even after a year without a US hurricane landfall for the first time in a decade, reflecting continued growth in property values and insured exposure in coastal and wildfire-prone areas. The 2026 European wildfire and drought season currently unfolding will likely contribute to upward revisions in subsequent editions.
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: RFC Power Closes £10 Million Series A and Rebrands as Certain Energy — British Business Bank Leads; Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust C3H Participate; Manganese Flow Battery LDES Platform Targets Grid-Scale Deployment
items.body_html: RFC Power, an Imperial College London spin-off developing manganese-electrolyte flow batteries for long-duration energy storage, closed a £10 million ($12.7 million) Series A on August 26 and simultaneously rebranded as Certain Energy. The round was led by the British Business Bank, which contributed £3.5 million, with participation from Centrica Energy, Ceres Power Holdings, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health (C3H). Certain Energy’s flow battery uses a manganese electrolyte — the 12th most abundant element in the Earth’s crust — and extends discharge duration by scaling electrolyte tank volume, enabling storage from hours to days without chemistry changes. The company plans to develop a grid-connected MWh-class demonstration system in India, expand its UK research facility, and build a supply chain for replicable utility-scale projects.
items.source_html: Renewable Energy Magazine / Solar Power Portal

items.title: Redstone Closes €25 Million First Tranche of Blue Economy Decarbonization Fund — Targeting Maritime Sector Carbon Reduction, Ocean Asset Security, and Coastal Infrastructure Resilience
items.body_html: Berlin- and Helsinki-based fund manager Redstone closed the first tranche of its blue economy decarbonization fund at €25 million during the week of August 28, targeting investments in technologies to decarbonize maritime sectors, secure ocean-based assets, and build resilient coastal infrastructure. The fund addresses a sector responsible for approximately 2.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions that has historically attracted less climate investment than aviation, trucking, or industrial processes. Alternative fuels (ammonia, methanol, green hydrogen), hull efficiency technologies, and port electrification represent core investment themes. The first close reflects growing investor interest in maritime decarbonization as the IMO’s strengthened 2050 net-zero shipping target creates regulatory pull for clean propulsion and alternative fuel solutions.

items.title: BlocPower Shuts Down and Liquidates — Community Clean Energy Electrification Platform Winds Down After 14 Years; Returns Capital to Investors
items.body_html: BlocPower, the community-focused clean energy company that electrified buildings in low-income urban neighborhoods by replacing gas heating and cooling systems with electric heat pumps and solar, is shutting down and liquidating its assets, returning remaining capital to investors. BlocPower had operated since 2012, achieving significant attention for its mission of decarbonizing community buildings in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and other markets. The shutdown reflects the persistent difficulty of achieving financial sustainability in community-scale energy efficiency retrofit businesses, which face thin margins, complex multi-party project execution, and slow payment cycles. The closure is a notable setback for impact-oriented community climate tech and underscores the structural challenges facing mission-driven platforms trying to deploy clean energy in underserved markets at scale.
